variants.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Make a preview sheet of FOUR ADULT HALF-BODY PIXEL ART portraits for a western harbor tavern game.
REFERENCE ROLES ARE CRITICAL: Image1 = exact identity, face, pose, outfits and REALISTIC ADULT ANATOMICAL PROPORTIONS to preserve. Image2 = ONLY reference for obvious crisp square pixel clustering and simplified flat material shading. DO NOT copy image2's large heads, large eyes or cartoon proportions. Image3 = target game environment palette and pixel context.
User correction: faces and bodies must be realistically proportioned, NOT CARTOON, NOT CHIBI, NOT CUTE BIG-HEADED CHILDREN. REDRAW image1 as clean deliberate PIXEL ART with the clearly visible pixels of image2, retaining image1's adult faces and body geometry. Head top to chin (excluding hat) must occupy ONLY about 24% of the head-to-belt height. Natural human small eyes, normal adult noses and jaws, long adult neck and arms, real shoulder width; Hank has old man's anatomy and a weathered face, Milo adult masculine proportions, the two women adult proportions. No oversized doe eyes, round baby cheeks, large foreheads or big heads.
Four separated columns, same scale, head and hat all visible down to waist/belt, elbows/hands inside canvas, plain muted dark brown background, generous margins. Order SHOPKEEPER / HANK / ADA / MILO, small labels along bottom. The version letter appears ONLY ONCE in upper left, NOT above each character.
Lock identities: white-haired shopkeeper with side braid, teal scarf, cream rolled shirt, brown fitted vest, compass pin, inventory paper; old Hank white moustache/grey side hair, dark cowboy hat, olive shirt, brown vest, cream scarf and hands resting together; Ada red braid/freckles, tan hat, muted blue shirt, brown vest, rust scarf, fingers touching hat brim; Milo dark hair/thin moustache/chin beard, brown hat, cream shirt, brown vest, rust scarf, hand on vest.
Keep poses and realistic proportions from image1. Simplify surface detail into large clean patches: only 3 to 5 tones per skin/fabric material, NO fine random texture, NO pores, NO dithering, NO weathered leather speckle, NO glossy AI skin. No smooth anti-aliased painting, no soft gradients. Angular pixel stairs on silhouette, coherent square pixel clusters, restrained warm side light matching image3. It must read as adult game character concept rendered in pixel art, not merely a blurred photograph. Only these four adults, no other characters.
Version A, single letter A top left. Relatively FINE but unambiguously visible pixel cells, roughly a 160-pixel-tall half-body with face around 38 pixels tall, uniformly enlarged. The whole frame should feel like a 512x320 pixel painting enlarged crisply. Fine clean clusters, retain subtle face character with limited colors. No texture noise.

Edit this entire four-person sheet into MUCH LOWER RESOLUTION hand-drawn pixel art. Keep EXACT same realistic adult head sizes, bodies, poses, faces, hairstyles, outfits, colors and layout. Rebuild every shape on a strict coarse square grid: each logical pixel is an obvious 6 by 6 display-pixel square, entire frame roughly 256x170 logical pixels enlarged 6x. Remove all microdetail; leather is smooth flat brown areas, skin has 3 flat tones, hair is big chunky locks. Strong obvious stepped curves and visible squares on noses and fingers. Natural SMALL adult eyes, realistic shoulder and head proportions. No cute or chibi anatomy. DO NOT leave any detailed painterly regions. Target old-school realistic-adult adventure-game portraits made of clean solid pixel clusters. Change upper-left A to B. Keep bottom names. Flat dark brown background, no gradient. This must look dramatically more pixelated and simplified than the input while retaining adult anatomy.

Edit this entire four-person sheet into EXTREMELY LOW RESOLUTION pixel art while LOCKING EXACT realistic adult anatomy and head-to-body ratios. Rebuild whole sheet as a 192x128 logical-pixel image enlarged 8 TIMES, so every single pixel cell is a BIG visible 8x8 square. No subpixel details. NO smooth painting. Max 16 flat colors in the ENTIRE sheet. Each head face has only about 10-14 logical pixels vertical but stays SMALL relative to the realistic adult body: do NOT enlarge heads to fit details. Face is built from very few colored squares: tiny natural eyes, minimal nose shadow, moustache blocks. Shirts and vests contain two flat colors each. Remove ALL skin texture, cloth texture and thin outlines. Keep hats, white braid/white moustache/red braid/dark moustache, scarves and body poses recognizable by silhouette. Exact same four-person composition, no cartoon exaggeration. Plain flat dark-brown backdrop. Change upper-left A to C, retain names in coarse pixel letters. This should look like a 16-color early adventure-game portrait, NOT a detailed illustration with a slightly pixel edge.

context.prompt: Create a two-panel wide pixel game portrait-in-environment concept, 16:9. Image1 is the exact character rendering/proportion reference, Image2 is the real game's warm sunset harbor tavern. LEFT panel shopkeeper waist-up holding inventory paper, in a timber harbor shop with shelves and crates. RIGHT panel elderly Hank waist-up hands resting together, in the tavern of Image2. Only one character per panel, each from Image1. Keep Image1's REALISTIC ADULT BODY PROPORTIONS: small natural heads, normal eyes, long arms, broad adult shoulders. Do not make them chibi or cartoonish. Keep exact pixel character drawing from Image1: obvious square clusters, simplified flat shading, 3 tones per material, NO high-resolution realistic textures. Preserve white braid, teal scarf, cream blouse, brown vest, compass pin; Hank grey moustache, brown hat, olive shirt, brown vest, cream scarf. Whole head/hat and belt visible in each panel, character height ~75% of image. Match the background's pixel size/color, background slightly subdued for readability but not blurry. Minimal clean dark gutter; tiny text SHOP and TAVERN only, no buttons/dialogue. This is a concept comparison, not a real screenshot. No other people.
